Minutes of a Called Meeting of the City Council.
Austin, Texas October 28, 1896.

Hon. Lewis Hancock, Mayor, presiding.
Roll Called.
Present, Aldermen Hayes, Horton, Nitschke, Platt, Pruell, Redd, Robindeau, Schneider,
Shelley and Zilger 10.
Absent Aldermen Deaty, Fischer, Glascock, Glass, North, Lawless, Linn, Rosengrin, Stumpf,
Taylor, Tobin and Townsend 13.
Alderman Schneider moved a call of the Council, which was ordered.
Aldermen North, Lawless, Rosengrin, Stumpf and Taylor entered the Council Chamber.
Alderman Schneider then moved to suspend the call, which motion prevailed.
The following call was then read:

Mayor's Office
Austin Tex, October 28th 1896.

Mayor's call for Special
Meeting

A special meeting of the City Council is hereby called to meet at 4:30 this afternoon at
the Council Chamber in the City Hall, for the purpose of considering an ordinance levying
taxes for the year 1896.

Lewis Hancock, Mayor.

City Marshals certificate
of serving call

Austin Texas Oct. 28th 1896, 3. P.M.
I hereby certify, that the following Aldermen have been served with the above call, by
having it read to each of them in person, viz: Deaty, Glass, North, Haynes, Horton,
Lawless, Linn, Nitschke, Platt, Pruell, Redd, Robindeau, Rosengrin, Schneider, Shelley,
Stumpf, Taylor, Tobin, Townsend and Zilger, and that Aldermen Glascock and Fischer have
been served by a true copy having been left at their last known place of residence in the
City.
James E. Lued, City Marshal.

Aldermen Deaty and Townsend entered the Council Chamber.
The Mayor then read the following message:

Mayors message on
Ord. fixing Tax levy
for 1896.

Austin, Tex., October 28th 1896.
To the Honorable City Council:
Gentlemen, I have called you to meet in Special session to consider the tax levy for the
ensuing fiscal year, for the reason that the usual time for fixing the tax rate has
already passed, it is urgent that it should be fixed, and it is desirable that you should
have this matter under advisement at once, so that you can settle it informally, at your

done this year, for the following reasons: 1st The dissatisfaction of many tax-payers with
the valuations fixed by the Board of Aldermisons, resulting in litigation over raises to
the amount of $1,319,450.00, has indeniably tied up the taxes whose property amounting to

It is therefore impossible to estimate accurately the amount which will be yielded by
taxation, or when it will be collected.
2nd Notwithstanding the vast sums extended by the City in the construction of its Water,
Light and Power Plant, it is notoriously in- complete. We have not yet an ample supply of
pure water, and it is certain that some additions to and changes in the machinery in the
Power house must be made to cure these defects. The balance in the Water and Light fund
has been gradually depleted by the payment of obligations contracted by preceding City
Councils, until it is now not more than $75,000.00, and it is possible it may be still
further reduced in the same manner. As I have not had the assistance of com- petent
engineering advice, I am unable to inform you what the necessary changes and improvements
in the Power house and Plant will cost, but I fear they will exceed the balance of
$75,000.00 in the Water and Light fund and may absorb all or nearly all the earnings fund
for the next year. It would be extremely satisfactory to me to advise the application of
the earnings of the Plant to the payment of the Interest and Sinking fund and a reduction
of the taxes to that extent, but, in my opinion, it is imperative that the Plant shall be
put in perfect working condition in order that its full earning capacity shall be
developed and proper service rendered to the public, and that this must be done at once,
even though by so doing, we delay much desired and much needed reduction in taxation.
Based upon the expenditures so far this year, the needs of the general fund next year will
be as follows: Salaries, Officers and Employees, $48,183.00

total estimated expenditure is $97,070.00. By rigid economy, this can and should be
reduced by $10,000.00, leaving a balance of $67,070.00 to be provided for. Of this sum the
Assessor and Collector estimates receipts from various sources, as follows: General
Revenue Tax, prior years; 5,000.00 License Tax, 9,000.00
Recorder's Court 7,400.00
Travis County, (Hospital) 7,000.00

Dog Tax 450.00

Total, $20,850.00
leaving the sum of $46,170.00 to be raised by taxation. Taking the tax rolls as they now
appear, the property subject to taxation amounts to $17,753,718.00, of which the sum of
$1,314,053.60 is in dispute on the ground of excessive valuations. Assuming that the City
will be finally sustained in half of this increased appraisement, amounting to $657,976.
the property subject to taxation would be $11,594,747.00, in round numbers $11,600,000.00.
Upon this valuation, a tax of forty cents on the hundred dollars would yield $46,400.00,
and a tax at that rate is therefore recommended for general revenue purposes. It is
probable that the delinquencies may reduce the proceeds of this tax to the extent of, say
$5000.00, in which case I should, though with reluctance, recommend making up that
deficiency out of the earnings fund.
The earnings of the Water, Light and Power Plant have amounted for the ten months of this
fiscal year to $43,018.03, of which $3,300.60 was paid by the City as one quarter's rent
for Water and Light.
Deducting this amount, we have $39,757.53, as the true earnings of the Plant for the ten
months. Upon this basis we may fairly estimate that the Plant will next year earn
$55,000.00. The operating expenses for the ten months have been $17,013.49, indicating
total operating expenses for the year of $15,000.00. I think this should, and will be
reduced for the next year to not more than $20,000.00, which would leave a net revenue
from the Plant of $35,000.00 to be applied to its necessary construction.
We must further provide for 5% Interest and 2% Sinking fund on $1,307,000.00 of Dam Bonds,
and 6% Interest and 2% Sinking fund on $700,000.00 of Dam Bonds, together amounting to
$108,890.00. A tax of 94 cents on the one hundred dollars will yield $109,940.00, and I
therefore recommend a tax of that amount for Interest and Sinking fund on Dam Bonds.

therefore recommend a tax of this rate to meet the Interest and Sinking fund on those
Bonds.
We must further levy a tax of 33⅓ cents on the hundred dollars for School purposes.
The total tax levy would then be as follows:
For General Revenue, .40
For Interest and Sinking Fund on $1,547,000.00 Dam Bonds, .94 For Interest and Sinking
Fund on Bonds issued prior to 1890, .10 For Schools, .33⅓
Total tax. $1.77⅓

This makes a total tax of One dollar and seventy-seven and one third cents on the hundred
dollars, and I recommend that the accompanying ordinance, providing for such levy, have
your careful consideration and be passed at your earliest convenience.
You will observe that I have omitted any provision for payment by the City out of the
General Revenue to the Earnings Fund for Water and Light consumed by the City for public
purposes.
As long as both funds are controlled by one body, this practice seems to me confusing and
useless. It is simply taking money out of one pocket and putting it in the other.
Respectfully,
Lewis Hadlock, Mayor.

The Mayor then laid before the Council an ordinance levying taxes for the year 1896, which
was read first time.
Alderman Glass entered the Council Chamber.
Alderman Dorth moved that the ordinance be referred to the Finance Committee and the City
Attorney, which motion prevailed.
On motion, the Council adjourned.
Jno. A. Johnson
City Clerk.
